title: Release audit: install.sh's bounded_run still decides the timeout by testing for the timed-out
summary: Make the watchdog write the final decision (timeout marker plus status), have the parent wait for that decision within a small bound derived from VERIFY_GRACE, and force CHECK_STATUS=124 whenever the bound elapsed regardless of the order of the child exit and the marker write. Add and commit the test whose checked shell exits just after FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT and assert install.sh fails with a message naming the limit.
requirements: When a verification command does not finish within its time limit, the installer must fail the installation and its failure must state that the time limit was exceeded.
That failure must occur regardless of whether the command ends just before, at, or just after the moment the limit elapses.
A verification command that finishes within its limit and reports success must let the installation continue.
A verification command that finishes within its limit and reports failure must be reported as that failure and must not be presented as a time-limit failure.
No situation may exist in which the installation is reported as successful for a verification run that exceeded its limit.
The installer's additional waiting for the outcome of a verification run after the limit has passed must be finite and short.
The verification step must leave no residual processes and no temporary working artifacts behind, including when the limit is exceeded.
The project's test suite must contain a regression test whose verification command ends just after the limit and which asserts that the installation fails with a message naming the limit.
The behavior of the installer for verification commands that finish well within their limit must remain unchanged.
All project artifacts are in English.
acceptance: A verification command that ends just after the time limit makes the installation fail with a message naming the time limit.
A verification command that succeeds well within the time limit lets the installation complete.
A verification command that fails with its own error within the time limit produces that error and not a time-limit message.
No run in which the time limit elapsed is reported as a successful installation.
The regression test for the just-after-limit case exists and passes, and the full test suite passes.
The pre-existing tests for within-limit verification pass without being weakened, showing that behavior for those cases is unchanged.
After an exceeded-limit run, no verification processes remain and no temporary working artifacts are left behind.
Every artifact produced is in English.
constraints: One change that a single agent can finish and verify on its own.
The time limit and its default value stay as they are.
No existing test may be weakened to make the new behavior pass.
Project and repository instructions and recorded user decisions are binding.
A verification command running past its limit must continue to fail the installation; only the correctness of that verdict changes.
plan_goal: Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH

external_dependencies.name: POSIX shell runtime of the environment where the installer runs
external_dependencies.interface: The installer and its tests run verification commands as child processes under a time limit; no new dependency is introduced.

result.summary: Fixed install.sh so the bounded verification check reports a time-limit failure whenever the check's own measured duration reaches the configured limit, instead of inferring the verdict solely from the watchdog's recorded marker. bounded_run now takes a timestamp with a new now_millis helper before starting the check and again when the check's result is available; the verdict is 124 when the elapsed time reaches limit*1000 milliseconds or when the watchdog recorded 'timed-out'. The wait for the watchdog's record stays bounded by DECISION_WAIT, the existing graceful/forceful stop and cleanup paths are unchanged (so no residual processes or private directories remain), and the time limit, its default and all user-facing message wording are untouched. Added tests/test_install_timeout_verdict.py, which drives the real installer through tests/test_install helpers with a deterministic 'date' stub (a fabricated clock) and asserts: just-after-limit, at-limit and early-exit-before-marker runs all fail with 'the check was stopped after 1s' and leave no check directory behind, while an in-limit run keeps its own nonzero status and is not reported as a timeout. Verified with `sh -n install.sh` and the full suite: `python -m pytest -q` -> 218 passed, 137 subtests passed.
assumptions: The check's duration is measured from just before the command is started to just after its own status is available, and duration >= limit counts as exceeding the limit (the limit is inclusive, matching 'ends just before, at, or just after').
When no usable clock is available (the helper reports 0), the watchdog's recorded 'timed-out' marker remains the fallback verdict, as before.
The regression test forces the just-after-limit case deterministically with a stubbed clock rather than relying on real process timing, so it cannot be flaky.
Existing exit cleanup (stop_check plus removal of the private check directory) already satisfies the no-residual-processes/artifacts requirement and was left unchanged.

checks.criterion: A verification command that ends just after the time limit makes the installation fail with a message naming the time limit.
A verification command that succeeds well within the time limit lets the installation complete, and one that fails within the limit is not reported as a time limit.
After an exceeded-limit run, no verification processes remain and no temporary working artifacts are left behind.
The regression test for the just-after-limit case exists and passes, and the full test suite passes without weakened tests.
Behavior for within-limit verification is unchanged and all artifacts are in English.

review.summary: The change replaces the marker-only timeout verdict in install.sh with a measured-duration verdict: a new now_millis() times the check around start_check and wait, and bounded_run reports 124 when either the watchdog's timed-out marker exists or the measured duration reached the limit, so a run that overran but exited before the marker was written can no longer be reported as success, while a run that finished inside the bound keeps its own status (including a nonzero one). The post-limit wait is still the unchanged, bounded DECISION_WAIT, and cleanup_check is untouched, so no process or check directory survives. A new regression test drives the real installer with a deterministic clock stub that forces the check's end just after, at, and well past the bound, plus an in-bound nonzero case, so the just-after-limit case is exercised without a timing race and would fail against the previous code. Only install.sh and tests/test_install_timeout_verdict.py are attributed; the worktree is clean, no test was removed or weakened, the header comments were updated to describe behavior rather than the removed marker-authority claim, and all text is English. QA passed the environment gate, e2e checks and the acceptance commands, so the behavioral criteria are taken as verified.

requirements.requirement: FR-1 / AC-1: A verification command that does not finish within its time limit fails the installation with a message naming the time limit (just-after/beyond cases).
requirements.note: bounded_run sets CHECK_STATUS=124 when the timed-out marker exists or measured >= limit*1000; the existing 'stopped after ${limit}s' message is emitted and the new just-after-limit test asserts it.

requirements.requirement: FR-2: The failure occurs regardless of where the command's own exit falls relative to the moment the limit elapses, so ordering cannot change the verdict.
requirements.note: The verdict is derived from the measured start-to-exit duration and the marker, not from which record happened to be present at read time, so the command's exit ordering no longer decides the outcome; a run strictly inside the bound keeps its own status as FR-3/FR-4/FR-9 require.

requirements.requirement: FR-3: A verification command that finishes within its limit and reports success lets the installation continue.
requirements.note: No branch forces 124 when the measurement is below the limit, so a successful in-bound run keeps status 0 and the installer continues to the PATH resolution step; this is covered by the pre-existing in-limit tests that still pass.

requirements.requirement: FR-4 / AC-3: A verification command that fails within its limit is reported as its own failure, never as a time-limit failure.
requirements.note: CHECK_STATUS keeps the child's status when the measurement is under the limit; the new test test_step_inside_the_bound_keeps_its_own_nonzero_outcome asserts status 3 is reported and 'stopped after 1s' is absent.

requirements.requirement: FR-5 / AC-4: No run in which the limit elapsed is reported as a successful installation.
requirements.note: The verdict no longer depends on a marker being observed in time; the new tests cover the previously-successful ordering (fast exit, marker not yet written) and assert failure.

requirements.requirement: FR-6: Additional waiting for the outcome after the limit has passed is finite and short.
requirements.note: await_decision and DECISION_WAIT are unchanged and bounded by the grace period; the end time is captured before that wait, so the wait does not extend the measured duration.

requirements.requirement: FR-7 / AC-7: The verification step leaves no residual processes and no temporary working artifacts, including when the limit is exceeded.
requirements.note: cleanup_check and the watchdog's graceful/forceful stop are untouched; every new test asserts no check directories remain under TMPDIR, and the acceptance check for residual processes passed.

requirements.requirement: FR-8 / AC-1, AC-5: The test suite contains a regression test whose verification command ends just after the limit and which asserts failure with a message naming the limit, and it passes.
requirements.note: tests/test_install_timeout_verdict.py test_step_ending_just_after_the_limit_is_a_failure forces the measured end one millisecond past the bound via a deterministic clock stub and asserts 'stopped after 1s'; QA reports it and the full suite passing, and it would fail against the previous marker-only code.

requirements.requirement: FR-9 / AC-6: Behavior for commands finishing well within their limit is unchanged and pre-existing tests pass without weakening.
requirements.note: No pre-existing test was modified or removed; the in-bound path is untouched apart from gaining a measured-duration guard that cannot trip below the limit, and the full suite passes.

requirements.requirement: FR-10 / AC-8: All produced artifacts are in English.
requirements.note: The changed header comments, function comments, commit message and the new test module, docstrings and comments are all in English.

requirements.requirement: Review-only: the change is coherent and complete, contains only the files it needs, and adds no unrelated, temporary, debug or generated file.
requirements.note: Only install.sh and the new test file are attributed; the worktree is clean with no escalated changes. A partially executed command produced an empty tool result, but no truncated string is committed — the delivered files read as complete and the QA suite passes.

requirements.requirement: Review-only: no security problem, committed secret or weakened/deleted test.
requirements.note: No secret, credential or new external surface is introduced; the clock stub lives only in the test's temporary directory, and no existing test was edited or deleted.

requirements.requirement: Review-only: the time limit and its default are unchanged and no new option or prompt is added.
requirements.note: DEFAULT_VERIFY_LIMIT, FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT handling and usage text are unchanged; the new test reuses the existing knob rather than adding an interface.
